cells.reference: TAR, no. 12/1086; Ibid, no. 45/1090; TAS, vi, no. 16, 25-6; KK, iii, no. 1968/255; also Kerala Society Papers series, 312
cells.remarks: Records a cash gift of 61 achchu by Guṇavaṇ Vadugaṇ alias Rājēndrachōlā-Vaiśravaṇnaṇ of Tirukkōṭṭāru alias Mummuđichōlānallūr Chōlākēralapuram to the temple of Rājēndrachōlīśvaram-Uđaiya-Nāyanār at the village. for providing for sacred food offerings cooked of five nāli of rice to the god Periyadēvar and his consort set up in the temple by the donor. The money was given to a Vīrapāṇ-điyap-Pallavaraiyaṇ and some land (measuring two mā and three kāṇi) was taken from him as iraiy-oṇri for cultivation by a Vadugaṇ Guṇavaṇ. It was stipulated that the latter should measure out the rice required for the service and that the dēvarkaṇmikal and māhēsvarakkaṇkāṇi-cheyvār should give daily to Kōmalavalli, a dēvarađiyāl of the temple and the younger sister of Vadugaṇ Guṇavaṇ, food of four nāli of rice from out of the above food offerings. It was further stipulated that the temple authorities should, in case of the redemption of the Oṇri land by Vīrapāṇ-điyap-Pallavaraiyaṇ, provide some other land by reinvesting the money on it and help Vađugañ Guñavañ to cultivate it hereditarily.

cells.remarks: Records a royal order granting some lands as dēvadāna-iraiyili (to the temple) inclusive of the kārāṇmai and mīyāṭchi rights. The grant was made on the representation of an Avyañ Maļavarāyan, the kēļvi of the king and the uļvari of the variyilār were issued to the effect that the grant be recorded on stone and copper. The taxes that were remitted on the lands included karupūra-vilai, kāriyav-ārāychchi vetti-ppātṭam, pānchupīli, sandivikkira-kappēru, ponvari, etc. Among the boundaries of the granted lands are mentioned Iraman-kulām, Kuđavai-kudiyi-ruppu, Kuđava-pallī, Šivalla-van-Pehuvāyakkāl and Karuṅgulām. The document is attested by Tiruvirāmīchcharam Uđaiyān Ātkonđavilli alias Kachchiyarāyan of Kaļattāvvūr in Chewirukkai-nāđu.

The location given in the KK is on the kumuda of the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Kōnērīsvara temple.

cells.remarks: Records a sale of temple land by the dēvakaṇmis of the Rājarāja-īŚvaram-Uđaiyār temple at Kalikkuli, a part of Kumari in Purattāya-nādu, a s.d. of Uttamachōlā-valānādu in Rājarājap-Pāṇdinādu to Nārppattenṇāyiravaṇ. The land was purchased by the latter for erecting thereon a water-shed called Jayangonđachōlāṇ. The land was lying to the south of the compound wall south of the shrine of Ayappaṇ Vēdiyachchāttaṇ situated in the south-east corner of the Rājarājīśvaram-Uđaiyār temple, to the north of the tank called Uttamachōlā-pērēri and to the west of the Peruvali going to the Chakkara-tūrttam from Kumari along the east bank of Uttamachōlā-pērēri. The sale-deed was written by temple accountant Arayaṇ- Kaṇdaṇ. Note: 1. The record has been assigned to Rājarāja II (?), by the editor of the KK. (no. 1968/111).

cells.remarks: Records an agreement given by the Perumakkal of the Rājarāja-Īśvaramtemple at Kalikkuđi in Purattāya-nāđu, a s.d. of Uttamachōla-valānāđu in Rājarājap-Pāṇdināđu to offer food offerings prepared with two nāļis of rice daily to the deity of the shrine of Tiruppēndīśvaram-Uđaiyār in return for the amount of 20 kāśu received by them from a merchant, called Āchchaṇ Mārṇili alias Pēndirttāṇ, of Kumari alias Gaṅgaikonđachōlapuram in Purattāya-nāđu. Mentions that Dēvakaṇakkaṇ Araiyaṇ Kurṇan wrote the document.

cells.king: Śrī Kōṇēriṇmaikonđān (and) Parakēsarivarman alias Uđaiyār Śrī Rājēndradēva (Rājēndra II)
cells.reference: ARE, 1896, no. 105; TAR, no. 33/1085; TAS, i, no. viiii (III), 164-8; KK, i, no. 1968/56
cells.remarks: Contains the short historical introduction Iratṭaippāđi ēlarai etc. of the inscription of the king. States that when the king was seated on the throne called 'Kāđuveṭti' in the hall 'chōla-Kēralaṇ' in Gaṅgaikonđachōla-puram he made the following gifts: (i) the income derived from the taxes on all the dēvadāna villages belonging to the temple of goddess Kanniyā-bhaṭāriyār at Kumari alias Gangaikonḍachōlapuram in Purattāya-nāḍu, a s.d. of Uttamachōlavalanāḍu, which was district of Rājarāja-Pāndi-nāḍu were endowed for the celebration of a special service on every Hasta nakshatra which was the natal star of Kilānaḍi, one of the queens of the king. (ii) the income derived from various taxes on all the dēvadāna villages of the temple Rājarāja-īSvaram in the same place was endowed for the services and offerings to the god of the temple. (iii) the revenue accrued from taxes on the villages of the śālābhōgam of the Rājarājaṇśalai at the same place were gifted for the upkeep of the same śālai. These gifts were coming into force from the fourth year of the reign of the king. The oral order issued by the king to this effect was drafted by the Tirumandira-ōlai officer Jayaṅkondachōla-Magadha-rājan, Tirumandira-ōlai-nāyakam Uttama-chōlakkōn, Rājarāja Brahmarāyan, Kālingarājan, Toṇdaimān, Tribhuvana-Vallabha Vanṇāḍudaiyān and Mūvēndar-Chōlakkandiruvap-Periyān. Then the officer * Villavarāyar and Kāḍuveṭtigal ordered certain adhikāris of uḍaṇkūṭtam to declare the villages tax-free and they did the same. The officials mentioned in the record are: Rājarāja-Malavarāiar, Rājarājachōla-Brahmarāyar, Jayaṅkondachōla-Velupparaiyar, Adhirājēndra-Mūvēndavēlār, Rājarāja-Anukkap-Pallavaraiyar, Tiruchchi-rṇambala-Mūvēndavēlār, Rājakēsari-Mūvēndavēlār, Mūvēndavēlār of Uttamachōla-Tiruvindalūr-nāḍu, Mahipāla-Vilupparaiyar, Alāgiyachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Kāli-Ādittakōn Rājēndi... Mūvēndavēlār of Jaṇanāthanallūr, Rāmanaśaṇi Olāgapattiraṇ alias Nṛipēndrachōla-Mūvēndavēlār of Paraśivamaṅgalam, Nārāyana-Mūvēndavēlār, Brahma-Pallavaraiyar, Śakkarapāni-Brahmaārappatṭtar Chōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Mummudichōlap-Pallavaraiyar, Jayaṅgondachōla-śēnāmugha-Mūvēndavēlār, Uttamachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Manukula-Mūvēndavēlār, Uyyakonḍachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Nittavinōda-Mūvēndavēlār, Kshatriya-śikhāmaṇi-Mūvēndavēlār, Gangaikonḍachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Udaiyamārttāṇḍa Mūvēndavēlār, Gangaikonḍachōlap-Pallavaraiyar, Pārthivēnda-Mūvēndavēlār Narapālatoṅga-Mūvēndavēlār, Rājarāja-Anuttirap-Pallavaraiyar, Aṛīnchigai-Vilupparaiyar, Abhimānamēru-Mūvēndavēlār, Madhurāntaka-Vilupparaiyar, Śingalāntaka-Mūvēndavēlār, Vikramachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Valavaṇ-Mūvēndavēlār, Vīrachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Sundarachōlap-Pallavaraiyar, Adula-Parākrama-Mūvēndavēlār, Alāgiyachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Pārthivēndra-Vilupparaiyar, Villavaṇ-Mūvēndavēlār, Vīra-Pāṇḍya-Mūvēndavēlār, Valudikulāntaka-Mūvēndavēlār Rājāditta-Mūvēndavēlār, Teluṅgukulakāla-Mūvēnda-vēlār, Jayaṅgondachōla-Mūvēnda-vēlār, Kiḍārangoṇdachōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Śrīkānda-Mūvēndavēlār, Mīnavaṇ-Mūvēn-dāvēlār, Olōga-Vijjādira-Mūvēndavēlār, of Rājēndra-Tirunlūrnāḍu1, Uttaramandiriyār, Nīṇamadichōla-Mūvēndavēlār, Valavakē-sari-Mūvēndavēlār, etc., the uļvari tiṇaikkalatti-kaṇkāṇi officers such as Kumaruvijādara-Mūvēndavēlān, Kōdaṇ-ṭarāma-Mūvēndavēlān, Adiśaya-chōla-Mūvēndavēlān, Mūvēndi śēra-Mūvēnda-vēlān, Jayaṅgondachōla-olōga-Vēlān, the puravari-tiṇaikkalam officers like Arindavan-Mūvēndavēlān, Vikkiramachōla-Pāndya-Mūvēndavēlān, Valavasundara-Mūvēndavēlān, Kuvaļaiya-Divākara Mūvēndavēlān, Dēvamaņgalamudaiyān, Sūratoņga-Mūvēndavēlān, Vīranārāyana-Mūvēndavēlān, the varippottagam officers like Vidārkaruđaiyān, Širrambalamuđaiyān, Sundarachōlanallūr-uđaiyān, he mugavetti officers such as Manarkkudiyān, Āndaikkilān, Šōlamādēvi-Uđaiyān, Vallamuđaiyān, Vadugakkuđaiyān, Malaiyūruđaiyān, the varippottaga-kaņakku officers like Sangattimaņgalamuđaiyān, Paruttikuđaiyān and other officers including one Vikramachūlāmani-Mūvēndavēlān.

cells.location: 1. Read Tiruvindaqur · Agattisvaram Taluk · Kanyakumari · Tamil Nadu
cells.findspot: On six cylindrical stone pillars in the manimaṇdapa in front of the central shrine in the same temple
cells.reference: EI, xviii, no. 4, 21-55; TAS, iii, 87-158; KK, i, no. 1968/79
cells.remarks: This long inscription after giving a lengthy mythical genealogy of the Chōlas, enumerates the achievements of the Chōla monarchs from Vijayalaya, who is said to have constructed a new city of Tanjapuri. The son of Vijayālaya was Ādityavarman alias Kōdaṇdarāma (Āditya I) who killed the Pallava king seated on his elephant. His son Parāntaka (I) destroyed the Pāṇdya king together with his army, took the whole of his treasure and burnt Madura, his capital and was known as Madhurāntaka. Because he defeated the unconquered Krishnarāja he came to be known as Vīra- Chōlā. He caused his army to cross the sea and conquer Simhalā. He is further stated to have constructed several agraharas like Vīranārāyaṇapura and granted them for the enjoyment of Brāhmaṇas. The son of Parāntaka(I) was Arindama. To Arindama was born a son named Parāntaka (II). Anticipating trouble from this valiant king, the Pāṇdya king fled across the mountains. Parāntaka (II) fought several battles and imprisoned a good number of kings. The son of Parāntaka (II) was Rājarāja. He caused a number of yāgas to be performed. It was the custom with Rājarāja never to kill those enemies who surrendered to him; in spite of this well-known fact the Chālukya king Satyāśraya senselessly ran away from the battle field. Rājarāja's son Madhurāntaka conquered the Kuntala king and made Manyakhēta, his capital, a camping and sporting ground for his army. Sending his generals at the head of his powerful army northwards, he caused them to defeat successively the kings of Kulūṭa and the Utkala countries and to kill the kings Kalinga and Vimśēndra (or Vaṅgīndra); and to bring the water of the Gaṅges filled in pots carried on the heads of the conquered kings. Madhurāntaka (i.e. Rājēndra I) had three sons, named respectively Rājādhirāja, Rājēndra-dēva and Vīrarājēndradēva. Of these Rājādhirāja, the eldest, destroyed the city of Kalyāṇapura and conquered the lord of that place, Āhavamalla. Rājādhirāja's successor Rājēndradēva was succeeded by Vīrarājēndra who killed the Maṇnata (Karnāta ?) kings in the battle of Kūṭal-śāṅgam. This king, Vallabhavallabha, took possession of Vēṅgi and Kalinga, left uncared for by his elder brothers and consequently overrun by enemies; Vīrarājēndra, known also by the names Karikāla and Vīra-Chōlā set up several Dharma-śāsanas. He presented an invaluable ruby, known as 'trailōkya-sāra', to the god Dabra-sabhāpati (the god of Chidambaram) and it was set up in the crown of that god. He established a number of agrahāras in the Chōlā, Tuṇḍira, Pāṇdya Gaṅgavādi and Kulāṭa countries and colonised with forty thousand brāhamaṇas well-versed in the Vēdas. The Tamil portion begins afresh with the phrase 'svasti-sri' and states that the king Rājakēsarivarmaṇ Vīrarājēndra, who bore the birudas and surnames Mahārājādhirāja, Rājāśraya, Rājarājēndra, Vīra-Chōlā, Karikāla-Chōlā, etc. granted lands in Naṇrirākkudi and Paruṅguḍi in Purattāya-nāḍu in Uttamachōlā-valaṇnāḍu for the daily services of the temple of Kaṇniyā-Pidāriyār at Kumari in Purattāya-nāḍu in Uttamachōlā-valaṇnāḍu.

cells.date: r.y. 9 :(First quarter of the 12th century A.D.)
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Tiruvalāra-jayamvalāra, etc. of the inscription of the king and recounts the acts of valour and piety donē by the king: He is said to have defeated the Chēra king and levied tribute from him. The king of the Kūpakas offered his daughter to Parāntakadeva in marriage. He fought a battle and took Viliṇām. He did the Kalamaṇuttal in śālai of Kāndalūr, listened to the requests of the 1,080 brāhmaṇas assembled in the Maṇiyambalam (hall), got the carp(kayal) engraved on the measure of weight and capacity after removing the old names and granted Tāyanallūr for the maintenance of 10 golden lamps set up by him in the temple of Anantapuram. He granted Purattāya-nāḍu to the family deity Teṇ-kumari-Kaṇṇi, for the purpose of feeding all those that attended her grand festival held annually on the Pushya nakshatra in the month of Tai. He took Kuļam from Teliņga-Vīmaņ and subjugated the Southern Kaliņga Country. The record proper narrates the boundaries of the dēvadāna lands as tax-free to the Kaņniyā-bhagavatiyār temple at Kumari in Puřattāya-nāđu, a s.d. of Uttamachōļa-vaļanāđu in Rājarāja-Pāņdināđu for food-offerings and unguents and for the celebration of the festival on the Tai-pūśam day, which was the kīng's birthday. The northern boundary of the said lands ran through Adiyaņūr, Peruņguđi-malai, Ānaimalai, Manuttirappāřai, Tōraņakuļi, Pidarāņēri-Koļukkuttu, Kaņdananeri-Koļukkuttu, Vāļai-yāřru-Vađavāru, Nāvāy, Kōđaikkalā, Viřakāđu-Kuppai, Oļukkantāļyu, Karuņgu-ļam, Allījyūr, Pūchanķuđi, etc. in Nāņchi-nāđu; the eastern boundary through Vichāpuri and Irukkantuřai in Karuņgula-vaļanāđu; the southern boundary passed through Maņarķuđi in Nāņchi-nāđu, Suchīndram, Kēraļakurichilr etc. (Other details are not available).

cells.findspot: On the inner wall of the second prākāra (back wall of Śivalippura) in the north-western corner of the Kanyā-bhagavati temple
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Putalamaṇdandai pugaluṭan, etc. of the inscription of the king. Records that the king when he was seated at the Pugalābāraṇan-maṇdapam in the palace at Madurai in Māḍakkulakkīl, granted at the request made by Araiyan Chōrān alias Śrīvallamārāyaṇ, a member of his kitchen establishment, the income realised for the antarāyam dues amounting to 50 kāśu from the village of Kōđalūr alias Kulāśēkhara-chaturvēdimangalam in Mēlvēmba-nāđu, a dēvadāna of the Tirunelvēli-uđaiyār temple, to the maṭha constructed by the king and attached to the temple of Kumari-Pirāṭī. The gift was to feed pilgrims on the festival day of Taippūśam. Necessary entries were made in the concerned tax-registers for which the uļvari official was sent to the temple along with the king's order. Four officers in the rank puravuvari-tiṇaikkaļa-nāyakam endorsed the grant along with Rājarāja-Viļupparaiyaṇ and Kālingarāyaṇ.

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Pūtalamađandai-pugaļuđaṇ mēviya etc., of the inscription of the king. The document refers to certain provisions made by the Pāndya king for feeding the mendicant pilgrims who attended the Taippūśam festival of the goddess at Kanyākumari. This is the uļvari (Revenue order) in respect of the mađappurām assignment. Out of the amount now remitted to Kōļalūr alias Kulāśēkhara-chaturvēdimangalam situated in west Vēmbanāđ, from the temple lands of the god and goddess of Tīrunelvēli, a sum of 50 kāśu shall be kept apart for feeding in the Kulāśēkhara hall attached to the temple of Kumaripirāṭtiyār, the mendicant pilgrims who attend the Taipūśsam festival of the goddess. With this money paddy shall be purchased at the prevailing price and the feeding commenced from the 3rd year opposite to the 9th.

cells.language: Tamil, Vatṭeluttu, 5 lines; some portions built in and incomplete
cells.remarks: Records that the sabhā of Kīlālmangalam, a brāhmadēva in Nāṇchi-nādu purchased some land for the temple of Madisūdana-viṇṇagar-Perumāṇ at their village. The land was to be used for providing sacred food offerings in the temple. It is said that a Kāīāmbichchēṭtar Kumaraṇ-Gōvindan of Val'kaninallūr in Ilādaippādi made some (cash) grant to make the land tax-free.

cells.findspot: On the north wall of the central shrine of the Vishnu temple
cells.reference: TAR, no. 6/1093; TAS, vii, 2-4; KK, iii, no. 1968/308
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Pumagaļ jayamagaļ etc., of the inscription of the king. States that one Śingan-Araṅgaṇ of Pachuṅgulam presented to the king, a petition of the śrīvaishṇavas, the priests (nambu-cheyvāṇ) and the officials of the temple of Puravari-viṇṇagar-Ālyār at Puravari-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in Nāñchi-nāđu requesting gift of some lands for worship and services in that temple when the latter was seated in the throne called Muṇaiyadaraiyaṇ in the palace-hall at Tirunelvēli in Kilvēmbā-nāđu. Accordingly the king granted 3/4 vēli and two 'mā of single and double crop lands free of taxes at Vīrakēralamaṅgalam, in Nāttaruppōkku.

text.remarks: Records that Dāmōdiran Kaṇdaṇ alias Vikramachōla-[Ānkuđi-Vēlāṇ] of Pirakil arranged that a Vilattūr-vēlāṇ Ānkuđimālālvāṇ should measure out six kalam of paddy per crop for providing daily two nālis of rice for offerings to the deity of the temple Puravari-viṇnagar-Ālvār on account of the land which he bought from the former. The land called Maṇnađi was situated in Kurakkōdu. The document was written by Vikraman-Āṇdāṇ of Pirakil.

At the instance of the ūr a vēlāṇ of the ūr wrote the deed.

cells.location: Puravaśēri · Agattisvaram Taluk · Kanyakumari · Tamil Nadu
cells.findspot: On slabs embedded in the base of the same temple
cells.reference: TAR, no. 65/1100; TAS, vii, 9-11; See also KK, iii, no. 1968/315; Ibid, no. 1968/314 & 316
cells.remarks: The first fragment refers to some gifts of cash (achchu) into the hands of Uchchil Nārāyaṇaṇ, the adikāram (officer) of the Puravari-Viṇṇagar-Ālyār temple for maintaining perpetual lamps. The second one dated in the Kollam 378 (c. A.D. 1203) refers to cash gifts to the temple for perpetual lamp and for provision of meals. The third fragment records gift of land by three persons called Araśu Kurūnguđi Irāmanaraṅgaṇ and Kāri-kāl to the temple as Tiruvāmoļi-vidaiyāṭtam (i.e., provision for recitation of the Tiruvāymoļi before the god). The land was situated in Kađaikai-paṭtanam in Kurū-nāđu. The fourth fragment mentions cash gifts made by some persons including one belonging Kurakkēni-Kollam and another person called Kurūnguđi-Tirumarūmārvaṇ of Vađachēri alias Mummuđichōļanallūr.

cells.reference: ARE, 1896, no. 85; EI, v, no. 6(E), 45; TAS, ii, 7
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Tirumagalpoļa, etc., of the inscription of the king. Records that when the mahāsabhā of Tiruchchivindiram a brahmadēya in Nānchi-nāđu, a s.d. of Rājarāja-vaļanāđu met in full strength in the tiruvagra-śālai the mūlaparađai-sabhā who were in charge of the śrīkāryam of the Mādēvar temple at the village and the parađaik-kuđiga! (cultivating tenants under the supervision of the parađai) expressed their inability to manage the temple affairs pay the iṛai (taxes) to the temple and handed over the charge to the mahāsabhā. The mūlaparadai-sabhā and the tenants agreed that if they transgressed the terms of their agreement they were liable to a fine of 15 kalāṇju of gold mahāsabhā appointed two vāriyar and one kaṇṇam to look after the temple affairs (dēva-kāriyam) and received in return some fixed remuneration.

cells.remarks: Records sale of land measuring 1/2 vēli and two mā to the temple of Paramasvāmi at Suchīndiram in Sundara-chōļa-chatur-vēdimangalam, a brahmadēya of Nānchi-nāđu in Uttamachōļa-vaļanāđu, by the sabhā of the village after receiving 60 kāśu as sale-price and tax-money. The sabhā exempted the land from taxes which they themselves undertook to pay off. They also resolved not to extract any kudīmai from the tenants of the land. The land was to be utilised for a service of sacred food offerings called Abhaiyākaran during the midday service and for the maintenance of gardeners looking after the flower-garden called Unnataraman, as intended by the donor of the cash, Veṇkāđaṇ Śānkaraṇ Śēnāpati Malaiyappichchōļaṇ of Uttama-chōļanallūr in Nallārĵr-nāđu in Rājādhirājā-vaļanāđu, a s.d. of Chōļa-manđalam. The same donor gave to the temple 50 sheep and 25 cows for lighting tow perpetual lamps and 5 more cows for supply of curd.

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Pūmagaļ-jayamagaļ, etc., of the inscription of the king. Records that when the king was seated on the cot called Muņaiyadaraiyaņ in the palace at Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaņgalam in Mulļi-nāđu, he ordered, on the representation of the sabhā of Suchindram alias Sundara-Pāndya chaturvēdimaņgalam in Nānchi-nāđu and a Nambi of Mānābharaņamaņgalam and Āņdapiļļai Bhaṭta Adhirātrayājiyār1, the grant of lands in a place called "Māligaimudalpađi" in Pulļamaņgalam in Purāttāya-nāđu to the temple of Mahādēvar at Suchindriam for meeting the required expenses of the services in the shrines of Kūttāđundēvar and Nambirāṭtiyār. The lands were granted as tax-free dēvadāna inclusive of the kārāṇmai and antarāyam. It is said that 20 mā lands in the same place which had been previously given away by the king's father to the temple of Tumburu-nārada-Īśvaram-uđaiyār at Iruk-kandurai in Purāttāya-nāđu were excluded from the present grant. 1. He is identified by the editor of this record with the author of the Grīhyaprayōga-vṛitti.

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Pūmaḍandaiyum Jayamaḍandaiyum, etc., of the inscription of the king. Records a gift of seven vēli of tax-free land inclusive of the kārānmai right to the temple of Suchīndram by the king praying for his long life. The gift was made on the occasion of the king's coronation when Nārāyaṇanĉhēndra alias Iđaiyārṇrumaṇgalattu-Nambi belonging to the Aśvalāyana-sūtra and Rāsitā-gōtra, Tirupputtūrālyār, Pillaiyār-Virakērala-dēvar and Uttaramantiri Virakērala-Pāṇdyakkōṇār were present. The land was situated in Adavōđu, near Pūchaṇkuđi in Purāttā-nāđu in Teṇ-Kūrū. The royal order for the grant was written down by the tirumandira-ōlai, Ambalvaṇ Nittavinōda-Mūvēndavēļār of Marāvaṇūr in Murāppu-nāđu. The kadaiyīđu was given by the Sēnāpatikal Chandirasēkharaṇ alias Virā-Pāṇdya-Mūvēndavēļār of Ilaveṇbai in Veṇbaikkuđi-nāđu. The uļvari was signed by the puravuvari-tīṇaikkala-nāyakam called Nārāyaṇaṇ Kēśavan Teṇṇava-sīkhāmaṇi-Mūvēndaveylar of Vilāttūr in Milalai-kūrṇam, the mukhaveṭti-nāyakam. Tāyaṇ Poṇnaṇ alias Kurumbil-udaiyāṇ of Araiyanēri in Šembil-nāđu and the kūrṇukku-kūrū Pērarulālaṇ Karṇanguđiyāṇ Vānavaṇ Valudikkōṇ of Kōṭtūr in Tiruvaljudi-valanāđu.

cells.remarks: Records endowment of land by the sabhā of Suchindram, assembled at the Tiruchchurṛru-maṇdapa in the temple of Suchindramudaiya-Nāyaṇār, for maintaining a perpetual lamp in the temple. A flower garden was also gifted on this occasion. Gōvindapraijñabhiṭarar was present in the assembly. It was decided that anybody found misappropriating the paddy dues from the lands should be fined three kalāṇju of gold by the supervising body of the day. The record was inscribed by the carpenter of the village, Padineṭtu-nāṭṭān Kulamāṇikkam alias Parpananā-pavāchāri.

cells.remarks: Records a deed of agreement(cheva-kaṇavōlaikaraṇam) drawn by the sabhā of Suchhīndram and the temple managing committee for maintaining the chariy of feeding three brāhmaṇas and providing sacred food offerings in the temple of Suchhīndram-Uḍaiyā-Nāyaṇār at Suchhīndram alias Sundarachōlapuram in Nāñchi-nāḍu, with the 200 new gold achchus endowed by Chokkattāndāl alias Ulagmul-udumuḍaiyāl, the queen of Perumāl Śrī-Vīrapāṇdya-Dēvar. They distributed the gold among three individuals, who were required in return to supply specified quantities of rice and who, if they fell in default, would have to repay the gold at the rate of 11/4 achchu per achchu they had received. The document was written by Kulamānikkan Tānu alias Padmanābāchāryan, the temple śilpāchāryaṇ.

cells.remarks: Records sale of land for Rājarājap-peruvilai to Kōṇkorṇaṇ Araiyaṇ alias Neriya-Mūvēndavēlār of Chirṇarachūr in Ārkatṭtuk-kūrṇam, on the south bank (of the Kāvēri) by the ūr of Tirukkōttāru in nāṇchi-nādu, a s.d. of Rājarāja-valaṇādu. The land was made over by the buyer to the temple of Pidāriyār Kommandai-Nangai at Vaḍachēri in Tirukkōttāru for providing food offerings thrice dāily, for bali offerings on the day of Rōhini. Kilavan keralan, Tekkil Mālōkkali and Appichađaiyan were the signatories to the documents.

cells.remarks: Vēnāđu; Vīra-Ravi-Uđaiyamārttān-đavarman Širaivāymārttavar of Kīlappērūr, r.y.——, Š. 1173, Kollam 426, Mesha 19 (expired), Thursday, Mūla-nakshatra, Bahula 5, Šivanitya-yōga and Varāhakaraṇa : (13 April. A.D. 1251) Records that when the king was staying in the Kōvikkal at Pudiyađam in Kēraļapuram-dēšam, he conferred the hereditary sthāna (right of kōyinma and Ūrāṇma) of the temple of Mahādēvar at Nayiṇār-Mutṭtalakkurichi alias Vīrakēra-lapuram on Iravi Kēraļavikrama-uđaiyār a Šaivāchārya Kāryattura Tambi, belonging to the kāniyāļar-kula, residing at Kōvikkal in Pūrvainka-viļākam in Kaṇnanūr-dēšam in Malai-manđalam with the following stipulations. Thenceforward he should collect the incomes from all sources according to the temple treasury, and defray, through the persons that perform the sacred duties in the said temple of the Mahādēva inclusive of the piļļaimār, all kinds of expenses such as those required for each day; those necessary for special occasions in each month and year as well as the expenses for conducting the annual festival falling on the day of Aśvati in the month of Kumbha without default in quantity or in time. Accounts of receipts and disbursements should be made out annually and the surplus amount left after meeting the expenses should be deposited. The parivaṭtam ornaments, vessels and utensils and all other kinds of property should be taken care of. The details regarding the conduct of the annual festival falling on the Vsati day are also given.

cells.dynasty: Vēnāđu
cells.king: Ravi-Kēralavarma-Tiruvađi
cells.date: Kollam 411, Jupiter in Vrīšchika, Mēsha, 27 day (expired) : (21 April, A.D. 1236)
cells.remarks: Old Malayālam; Vatţeljuttu, 99 short lines Vēnāđu; Ravi-Kēralavarma-Tiruvađi, Kollam 411, Jupiter in Vrīšchika, Mēsha, 27 day (expired) : (21 April, A.D. 1236) possession of the members of assembly and the ūrār of Kōlānallūr. It is said that during droughts, a reduced assessment, amounting to a fifth only, of the usual rates must be collected; and even from this quantity, 73 parai of paddy, required for the expenses of bahīttavritti and Ōṇam had to be deducted and the balance realised as an additional charge on the lands which had borne crop in the season. Arakkal and Sāral mentioned in the inscription, refer evidently to the two instalments in which the annual land assessment appears to have been paid. They seem to have been fixed with reference to the harvest and were perhaps paid in Kumbham and Kanni (as at present). The term taravu is used in the inscription first in the sense of a 'receipt' and secondly to denote a document. It corresponds to the term tiītu of other records. 1. Now kept in the Padmanābhapuram Museum.

cells.date: (12th century A.D.)
cells.remarks: —— :(12th century A.D.) Records the regulation of the sacred arrangement made in the temple by Nirāṇñapādā-paļāra-Tiruvađi; thenceforth the greatmen (priests) of the inner shrine should eschew wearing of grulled cloths, should wear only pavitram; in the maṭha, feeding persons who had not been following the ancient practice(kīliyakkam) must be discontinued; worship in the inner shrine should not be made without offering of rice with ghee, flower and sandal paste; the chewing of betel leaves in the presence of the Paļārar-Tiruvađi (Bhaṭārar-Tiruvađi) should be avoided; if the greatmen of the mēlśānti (i.e. those who conduct worship) did not observe these rules, they should be liable to a fine of 24 kāṇam of gold, the other transgressors being liable to a fine of 24 nāļi of rice.

cells.language: Sanskrit and Tamil; Grantha and Tamil2
cells.king: Karunandađakkar
cells.date: r.y.— :(Last quarter of the 9th century A.D)
cells.reference: : TAS, i, no. xiii, 197-200; PCP, A.19-23
cells.remarks: The Sanskrit portion after invoking the gods Brahmā, Vishṇu and Śiva, breaks off at the part where it begins to trace the genealogy of the Yādavas, to whose race the donor-king of the document probably belonged. The available Tamil portion on the second plate mentions a gift of land by Udāravīraṇ alias Chōrakañ-Chēndan of Kađigaipattanam with the stipulation that his descendants themselves should cultivate the land and pay the god's half(dēvaṇ-Kīl-Pādi). Another piece of land along with the head-channel was granted by a Chūlmann-udaiyān. Then the share-holders of the village (ūr-paṅguđaiyār) are mentioned; Nārāyaṇaṇ Gōvindaṇ of Vātāpi; Paramēśvara-bhattar of Iđaitturai; Gōvinda-Bhattar of Vyariyam; Kūđatilāvi-Yajnan; Pāṇdan Śaṅkaran of Karaiūr; Chēndan-Nāgan of Mullaiūr; Tatantuppaṇ of Nāyttōđu, Talaimaṇai-Nāgaśanman, Śaṅkaraṇ Śaṅkaraṇ of Maṭram, Chēndan Śaṅkaraṇ of Naychittamaṅgalam, Pūndurutti-Kumaraṇ Achchutan of the same village ūr and Maṇiyaṇ-Kaṇdaṇ of the chēri of the same village; Kaṇda-Nārāyaṇaṇ of Perumalūr; Chađaiyaṇ Nārāyaṇaṇ, Valamburichchēri-Chađaiyaṇ Nārāyaṇaṇ Kaṇdaṇ Tuppiramaṇiyaṇ, Sarvvakrattu-yāji Akki, Śaṅkaraṇ Chađaiyaṇ and Kađambaṇ Tāyaṇ of the same Perumalūr village; Nārāyaṇaṇ Chakkirāpaṇi, Nakkaṇ Mādāvaṇ and Aṅgitāyaṇ of Kōđanūr; Kaṇdaṇ Chāttaṇ of Veṅgūr; and Śiritarankumaraṇ of Nīrvāṇūr. The Officer incharge of the village (ūrudaiyāṇ) was Kannaṇchāttaṇ of Arupūṇai-Mūttukōđu in Valluva-nāđu. The document was written by Aviyalanṇrađakkaṇ alias Śrīvallavap-perumbaṇaikkaṇ of Viliñam, who was the manufacturer of weapons (āyudaṅgal-Chēyvāṇ) to the king Karunandađakkar. Note: 1. These two copper-plates bound together by a ring were found in the Śiva temple at the village. These plates are the first and last ones of a set, the middle plates of which are lost. The first side, of the first plate is engraved on the inner or the second side only, while the second plate has writing on the first side only.2. The pulli is marked in several instances.

text.remarks:
The Sanskrit portion after invoking the gods Brahmā, Vishṇu and Śiva, breaks off at the part where it begins to trace the genealogy of the Yādavas, to whose race the donor-king of the document probably belonged. The available Tamil portion on the second plate mentions a gift of land by Udāravīraṇ alias Chōrakañ-Chēndan of Kađigaipattanam with the stipulation that his descendants themselves should cultivate the land and pay the god's half(dēvaṇ-Kīl-Pādi). Another piece of land along with the head-channel was granted by a Chūlmann-udaiyān. Then the share-holders of the village (ūr-paṅguđaiyār) are mentioned; Nārāyaṇaṇ Gōvindaṇ of Vātāpi; Paramēśvara-bhattar of Iđaitturai; Gōvinda-Bhattar of Vyariyam; Kūđatilāvi-Yajnan; Pāṇdan Śaṅkaran of Karaiūr; Chēndan-Nāgan of Mullaiūr; Tatantuppaṇ of Nāyttōđu, Talaimaṇai-Nāgaśanman, Śaṅkaraṇ Śaṅkaraṇ of Maṭram, Chēndan Śaṅkaraṇ of Naychittamaṅgalam, Pūndurutti-Kumaraṇ Achchutan of the same village ūr and Maṇiyaṇ-Kaṇdaṇ of the chēri of the same village; Kaṇda-Nārāyaṇaṇ of Perumalūr; Chađaiyaṇ Nārāyaṇaṇ, Valamburichchēri-Chađaiyaṇ Nārāyaṇaṇ Kaṇdaṇ Tuppiramaṇiyaṇ, Sarvvakrattu-yāji Akki, Śaṅkaraṇ Chađaiyaṇ and Kađambaṇ Tāyaṇ of the same Perumalūr village; Nārāyaṇaṇ Chakkirāpaṇi, Nakkaṇ Mādāvaṇ and Aṅgitāyaṇ of Kōđanūr; Kaṇdaṇ Chāttaṇ of Veṅgūr; and Śiritarankumaraṇ of Nīrvāṇūr. The Officer incharge of the village (ūrudaiyāṇ) was Kannaṇchāttaṇ of Arupūṇai-Mūttukōđu in Valluva-nāđu. The document was written by Aviyalanṇrađakkaṇ alias Śrīvallavap-perumbaṇaikkaṇ of Viliñam, who was the manufacturer of weapons (āyudaṅgal-Chēyvāṇ) to the king Karunandađakkar.

Note: 1. These two copper-plates bound together by a ring were found in the Śiva temple at the village. These plates are the first and last ones of a set, the middle plates of which are lost. The first side, of the first plate is engraved on the inner or the second side only, while the second plate has writing on the first side only.2. The pulli is marked in several instances.

cells.date: r.y.——, Mēsha, Jupiter in Tulā; (c. 12th century A.D.)
cells.remarks: Records gift of some land situated in several plots having the total showing capacity of one kuṇuñi and five nāļi of paddy, by Uđaiyan Paṇṇādi and Uđaiyan Maṅgalanangai of Marudattūr in Kuru-nāđu, to the temple at Tiruviđaikkōđu, for providing sacred food offerings and for feeding seven brāhmaṇas in the temple on the day of Dvādási of the bright fortnights. Those who supervised the cultivation (adikārikkuavaragaļ) were asked to conduct the services as required by supplying the necessary articles for the same from the proceeds of the land. For every occasion of default, double the quantity at default was to be levied, for two occasions the levy of an additional fine was also fixed and for three occasions; the ūrār of Marudattūr and the temple servant, were empowered (after cancelling the previous agreements) to conduct the charity themselves. The taxes on the land were remitted by transferring the burden to some other lands.

cells.findspot: On the four sides of a dressed pillar set up outside a ruined Siva temple
cells.date: Kollam 354, Vrīśchika 8, Thursday, Mūlā :(3 November A.D. 1179)
cells.remarks: States that when the king was staying in a flower-garden to the east of Tiruvāṭṭāru, he made a gift of land called "Chemmūdaimāmpallam" in Killiyūr to meet the expenses of worship in the Pirayisvaram-udaiya-mahadeva temple at Killiyur. The necessary document (cheyakađavōlai-karaṇam) was drawn up jointly by the officials (kāriyañ-cheykiṇravarkał) of Vēnāđu and of the local nadu. One Śēkharaṇ Kumaraṇ of Vayakkalūr who obtained cultivation rights of the land was directed to supply the quantity of paddy towards the mēlapādi (owner's share) for the temple in the hands of the temple priest and the vāriyaṇ. The tirumugam of the king and the temple document (kōyir-kuri) were given to this effect to the perumakkał of the Áśramam for getting them inscribed on stone in the temple.

cells.remarks: The inscription consists of two parts, of which the first gives details of an income of 67 achchu set a part for feeding persons on dvādāsi days of the 12 months of the yeañ. Provision is made only for 17 dvādāsis. This portion is said to have been engraved on copper-plate in the month of Tulā of the year in which Jupiter was in Kumbha. The second part registers gifts made for feeding on other occasions such as Tiruvōnam, Pūṇṇima, Ayana-śaikrānti, Pradpat and birth or anniversery days of some of the persons.

cells.findspot: In the same place (proper right of entrance)
cells.remarks: Malayālam; Vatṭeluttu, 4 long lines —— :(11th century A.D.) Records that, when Jupiter stood in Vrīśchika, in the month of Simha, the perumakkaļ of Pārttivaśēkharapuram (Pārthivaśēkharapuram) having met on the bank of the tank of the temple at Kulachchai granted unanimously (avirō-dattāl) a garden land(purai-yiḍam) as atṭtilpēru to Kēralaṇ-Ādichchavaṇmaṇ alias Irāyādarāya (Rājādhirāja)-Valluvanādālvāṇ of Kāritturai. The grantee was asked to maintain a perpetual lamp in the shrine of Ālyār at Pārthiva-śēkharapuram as rakshā-bhōgam. The granted land was invested' with the same immunities as obtained within the tiruchchuṇmunaṇ-dapam. The land was situated to the south of tank of the temple of Kulachchai, to the west of Pādakachchēri-valā and Maṇar-palli-mulvilai and the west of the stone called Chemmarippārai in the fort of Paralaiyūr. The patipēdamūla and the ūr of Kulachchai were enjoined to protect the fort (of Paralaiyūr ?). If any inhabitant (or cultivator) of the grant land committed a crime he should not be punished by any body living in the fort; he should not be treated according to the non-prevailing within the tiruchchuṇmu-maṇdapa. The ūr of Kulachchai were assigned a mā of land yielding 20 kalam from which one-third of the income, exclusive of the pulaikkāval was allowed to be enjoyed by them.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|viii||533" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. VIII, No. 533</button>
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land by Pugalttunai-Viśaiyaraiyaṇ to god (Tiruvađiga!) of the temple at Tiruvallikkēni for providing food offerings during night. The land called Karumārachchērippulam which had been mortgaged by the kulaṅgilavarga! thereby causing shortage of 45 kāđi of paddy and the discontinuation of the offerings, was redeemed and made his own by the donor (i.e. Viśaiyaraiyaṇ) after paying 30 kādis of paddy and five kalaṇju of gold. Śaṅgaśarman, Śaṭtiśarman and younger Śaṭtiśarman were to conduct the night offerings daily to god using two nāli of clean pounded rice made from five nāli of paddy, which was fixed as the interest on 45 kāđi of paddy. For failure to do so, it is stated that, the priest would have to present the offerings out of the shares in the plots of Avvi, Dattaṇ and Kārai-kilāṇ. The īla-lamp, the cup (Vaṭtil) and the metal pot(probably gifted by the same donor) were also entrusted to the care of the priests.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="are" data-key="are|1955-56|b|204" data-url="ARE-Inscriptions.html">ARE 1955-56, App. B, No. 290</button>
cells.remarks: Commences with the mention of a place by name Kuļumbūr and of the chief Pallivelan who probably fell fighting, apparently in an encounter at the place. Parāntakap-Pallivēļān, son of Pallivēļān is stated to have served in the campaign at Idavai. The former's son (i.e., Parāntakap-Palli vēļān's son) Andavēļān Kurumbar-Ādittaṇ Pulla-Nakkaṇ served Mahārājar Kōch-Chadaiya-Mārar. He was associated with the king in the campaigns at Viliṇam, Idavai and Tirukkudamūkku. Pulla-Nakkaṇ's son was Pallivēļān Nakkam-Pullaṇ whose activities are then described in greater detail. In this connection are mentioned Simhaļarāja, Śālāgrāme, a Varaguṇa-Mahārāja who is described to have killed a huge elephant whose name appears to be Ayirāvaṇam and lastly Śennilam. Pallivēļān Nakkam-Pullaṇ is stated to have led nineteen elephants to the battle field at the last mentioned place. The record then recounts how the king honoured Nakkampullaṇ highly by bestowing on him gifts for his services and conferring on him the title Kumaraṇ. Then Nakkam-Pullan and his son are stated to have made a gift of land to a person whose name ends with Tirumalai.

cells.remarks: Records that Māraṇgāri alias Vaidyaṇ Mūvēndamaṅgalap-pēraraiyaṇ of Kaļakkuḍi, the Prime-minister (uttara-mantri) of king Māraṇijaḍaiyaṇ who constructed this stone temple, died without consecrating it. His younger brother Māraṇ Eyiṇaṇ alias Pāṇdimaṅgalaviśaiyaraiyaṇ who succeeded him as Prime-Minister, consecrated the temple, after raising the muga-mantapam (mukha-maṇtapa). Māraṇgāri of this record is given the title Madhurakavi in the previous one. (Mdu.:10). This title has led to an assumption that he had some connection with the Vaishṇava Ālyār Kāri Māraṇ alias Nammālvār the author of the Tiruvāymaļi. For the identification of kalakkuḍi with Ukkirankkoṭtai in the Tirunelveli taluk, see EI, xxiii, no.45.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxii|i|39" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXII Pt I, No. 39</button>
cells.match_text: SII Vol. XXXII Pt I, No. 39
cells.remarks: Records that an adhikāri (officer) of the king called Aruṇidhi Kaliyan hailing from Marudūr in Puṇangarambai-nāđu, a s.d. of Chōla-nāđu bought a tank with two velis of wet land irrigated by it from the temple of Narasingaperumāṇađigaļ on the Tiruvāṇaimalai hill. The temple had been paying 18 īlakkāśu as tax on its entire lands to the sabhā of Narasingamaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Kīliraniyamuṭṭam. The Land bought by the Arunidhi Kaliyan owed 1/3 of the tax i.e., six īlakāśus. To make the land tax-free he paid to the sabhā 15 īlakāśu as īraikāval and made over the land to the sabhā who undertook to provide sacred food offerings during the three services in the temple using one-half of the produce (i.e., 150 kalam of paddy) and to feed five brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Vēdas in the same temple. The charity was to commence from the day when an almost total solar eclipse occurred on the asterism of Āślēsha corresponding to the Friday in the month of Karkaṭaka in the thirty-third regnal year of the king.

cells.remarks: Records that the affairs of the stone temple named Śrīkaṇṭhēśvaram constructed by Teṇṇavaṇ-Šāttaṇ for the Bhaṭāra at Tirumāttūr were examined (ārāyaniṇṛu) by this officer, and that the wet and dry lands belonging to the temple priests (aganāligaiyār), drummers, etc., situated in Birundaivūr were also properly checked and regulated.1 Note: 1. The fact that the old dēvadāna lands were checked in the time of Vīra-Pāṇdya indicates that the temple was functioning from earlier times, presumably as a brick structure, and that it was now rebuilt in stone (tirukkarrali-edutta) by this chieftain, with the new name of Śrīkaṇṭhēśvaram after his own name Kaṇdaṇ, and the flower garden called 'Sōlāntakan' was endowed in the name of the king himself.

cells.remarks: Connected with the previous inscription (Mdu.: 79). Records that the māhēs-varak-kaṇkāṇi-cheyvār of the Tiruvālavāy-uđaiya Nāyaṇār temple assigned Māttūr, the eastern hamlet of Kođimaṅgalam and a dēvadāna of the above temple to Mādēvar Alagiya Chokkaṇār alias Sundara-Pāṇdiya-chchōlakkōṇār, a kaikōla of the temple of god Uđaiyār Vāduśeydavāraṇamuđaiya-Nāyaṇār as kārānmai-kāṇi after receiving the karpūra-valai from the latter. The purchaser had to reclaim the land at Mattur for cultivation and pay annually to the temple as kađamai as follows: for the first year after reclamation four kalam of paddy per mā; for the second year six kalam; the third year eight kalam; the fourth year ten kalam; the fifth year 12 kalam and from the sixth year fifteen kalam.

cells.remarks: Records royal gift of Puravuvarinallūr for bathing service to the god Tiruvālavāyuḍaya Nāyaṇār. Puravuvarinallūr alias Chētuvāyattanallūr in Anđa-nāđu was the kāṇi of Kariyamāṇikkālvān Tiruvuđaināyagar alias Vīra-Pāṇdya-Kālingarāyar of Kāppalūr alias Ulagalantachōlanallūr in Muttūrruk-kūṭram. The bathing service was instituted by the king in his name. The gift village was required to pay the temple annually as vādāk-kađamai a sum of forty poṇ for the service.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||51" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 51</button>
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 50 cows for a lamp to god Tirumērrali Bhatāra at Peruntēṇūr in Pāgaṇūr-kūrram by Vēlāṇ Araiyaṇ of the village.1 Note: 1. The pillar which bears this record apparently was part of the temple, ruins of which are noticed in the site. Though Tirumērrali may signify a temple of Vishṇu, for Vishṇu temples are generally located in the west of the village and are called as such, a neglected liniga found in the locality indicates that the original temple may have belonged to god Śiva. In some places Śiva temples have also been called 'Tirumērrali'.

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Tirumađandaiyum, etc., of the inscription of the king. Records that when the king was seated on the throne Pānđiyarājaṇ in the hall called Alagiya-Pānđyaṇ-kūđam in the palace at Madurai, his officer Kālingarājaṇ represented that certain dēvadāna lands of the Tiruchchakkarattālvār temple may be given as kuđinīnga-kārānmai to Šrī Harushaṇ-Nārāyana-Bhatta-Vājapēyayājin 'sarvakratukkal of Kīraṇŭr a sixth chēri of Chōlāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya of Pāgaṇŭr-kūřram. The king condescended to the request and fixed the taxes payable by him. Among the boundaries of the land, a stone-dam called Parākrama Pānđiyaṇ-Kallanai, Vīra-Pānđiyaṇ-kāl, Šrīvallabhappērāru, and Parākrama Pānđiyaṇ kattaļai are mentioned. Note: 1. This royal order issued in the name of Kōnēriṇ-maikonđāṇ and relating to the same transaction, is engraved in continuation of the above inscription.

cells.remarks: Part A of the inscription begins with the historical introduction Tirumađan-daiyum jayamađandaiyum, etc., of the inscription of the king and records a royal declaring the reconstitution of some dēvadānta lands with the name Kulaśēkharamaṅgalam1 in the 11th year of the king, on the request of Kālingarājaṇ, when the king was in the palace at Chōlāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalamin Pāgaṇŭr-kūřram. The said lands were endowed as tax-free to the temple of Tiruchchakkarattālvār at Chōlāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam by one Chittakutti Mādavaṇ alias Chōla-Muttaraiyaṇ of Māngadu in Māngāđu-nāđu, a s.d. of Puliyŭrkōttan, after buying the same from the sabhā of the village in the second year of the king's reign. Some of these lands which were to the north bank of the river Vaigai were asked to be exchanged from similar lands on the south bank. This document was signed by Uttara-mantri of Perumaṇalŭr in Anda-nāđu and Kumaṇarāja. Part B of the record mentions the registration of the above transaction in ulyari (tax-register) in the 11th year of the king. This part was singed by Śrīvallava Uttara-mantri and Vēlān Āliyungaiyu of Vēlmaṅgalam, the mugavetti of Puravu-vi-tiṇaikkaļam. 1. The name Kulasēkharamaṅgalam implies that a Pāndya king named Kulasēkhara was a near contemporary of Śrīvallabha.

cells.remarks: This consists of three parts. The first one records a royal order issued by the king from his palace at Madurai to the east of Māṭakkuļam. It states that some lands endowed by Chittaka Mādavaṇ of Māngādu in Māngādu-nādu of Puliyūr-kōṭtam in the 11th year of the king to the temple of Tiruchchakkarattālyār at Śrī Chōlāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Pāganūr-kūrram were cultivated by one Śarvakratukkaļ by digging a new channel. This digging of the new channel was objected to by the sabhā of the village, who sold those lands previously. The grievance was carried to the king's presence by Kālingarāyaṇ who asked to grant some other lands in exchange on the other bank of the river Vaigai and requesting the remission of antarāyan on the lands for four years from the 16th regnal year of the king and the king proclaimed his order rectifying the defects brought to his notice. The second part records the royal communication to the Śrīvaishnavas of the Tiruchchakkarattālyār temple informing the above new arrangement. The third part records the subsequent communication of Kālingarāyaṇ to the Śrīvaishnavas and the dēvakaṇmis of the above temple1 1. The previous details of the same transaction are recorded in no. Mdu.: 313

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|v||294" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. V, No. 294</button>
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction Tirumaṇdandaiyum Jayamaṇdandaiyum, etc., of the inscription of the king. Registes gift of land as dēvadānaīraiyili for certain festivals and services in connection with the worship of the deities Kuttāđumdēvar and his consort set up in the temple of Śrī Mūlasthāṇamuḍaiyār at Chēndanērikkattīkkallūr by certain brāhmaṇas of Chōllntaka-chatur-vēdimaṅgalam in Pāgaṇūr-kūrram. The land originally, a brahmadēya belonging to the above brāhmaṇas was converted as dēvadāna-īraiyili by the king at the instance of Kalingattaraiyaṇ. The deed was announced by the Puravu-vari-tīṇaikkaṭattār when (they were) seated on the pallīkkattīl called 'Pandyarajan' in the hall called 'Alagiya-Pāndiyaṇ kūđam' situated in the ullālai of the temple.

cells.location: Ayyampāļaiyam · Palni Taluk · Madurai · Tamil Nadu
cells.findspot: Engraved over the natural cave in the hill
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xli||478" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XLI, No. 478</button>
cells.remarks: The Vatṭeĵuttu labels incised below the images of Jaina Tīrthaṅkaras sculptured in bas-relief over the cavern, palaeographically belong to the 9th century A.D. The inscription no. 700/1905 gives a date presumably in Śaka' era, of which only 700 (in words) could be read. The labels give the following names of the persons who made the respective sculptures found over them: Vichchi Varadapāṇi of Vaḍapallī Āram, Ajjaṇanda Indraśēna, Muvēndan, an inhabitant of Nālgūr in Vēmbu-nādu, Āri of Tiruvarambam, Mallisēnap-periyān of Vīrasaṅgattupperumaḍai, Kavirichchi: Nāgaṇ, Kāḍaṇ..., and Avvaṇandikkurattiyār. Two labels record gifts of gold respectively by an inhabitant (name lost) of Koĵumam and Svikitii Vaṭtam Vaḍugai, goldsmith of Kuvanachchēri. The god of the hill is said to be Ayiraimalai-Dēvar.1 Note: 1. No. 699/1905 which is written in a more archaic script, belonging to the seventh century A.D. is very much damaged.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|iii|iii|206" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. III Pt III, No. 206</button>
cells.match_text: SII Vol. III Pt III, No. 206
cells.remarks: In the family of the Moon, after many kings of great deeds had expired, came forth a son of Jayantavarman, the great king Arikēsari Asamasaman Alaṅghyavikrama Akālākal Māṛavarmaṇ. His son was on who fought battles at Marudūr and Kuvaļaimalai. (Here comes a break and one or two plates on which the genealogy should have been continued are lost). What is left on the last plate treats only of the description of the boundary line of the grated land or village and mentions the Bhagavati temple of Korranputtūr. The anatti of the grant was Tāyaṇ Singaṇ the Uttaramantri of Kunđūr in Kunđūr-kūrram of Anđa-nāđu. The Puranakāva of this village was eight five kaļam of paddy. The king himself, as in the Vēļvikkuđi grant, made a declaration and caused the copper-plate grant to be executed. The record was written by Arikēsari, son of Pāndi-Perumbanaikkāraṇ (who also wrote the Madras Museum plates).

The anatti of the grant was Tāyaṇ Singaṇ the Uttaramantri of Kunđūr in Kunđūr-kūrram of Anđa-nāđu. The Puranakāva of this village was eight five kaļam of paddy. The king himself, as in the Vēļvikkuđi grant, made a declaration and caused the copper-plate grant to be executed. The record was written by Arikēsari, son of Pāndi-Perumbanaikkāraṇ (who also wrote the Madras Museum plates).

cells.match_text: SII Vol. III Pt III, No. 206
cells.remarks: The Sānskirt portion after mentioning the mythical members of the Pāṇdya family states that in the family was born Arikēsarin. His son was Jaṭila; his son Rājasimiha; his son Varaguṇa; and his son Śrimāra entitled Śrīvallabha. Śrimāra conquered Māya-Pāṇdya, the kings of Kērala and Simhala, the Pallava and the Vallabha. His son was Parāntaka, the younger brother of Varaguṇa(II) who fought a battle at Kharagiri and captured Ugra. His wife was Vāṇavaṇmahādēvi and their son was Rajasimiha. The Tamil portion enumerates the genealogy of the king as follows: After many kings had passed away there came a king named Parānkuśa who saw the back of the Chēra king at Nelvēli and the Pallava king at Śānkaramaṇgai. His grandson was Rājasimiha after whom came a king named Varaguṇa Mahārāja. Rajasimha's son was Parachakrakōlāhala who was successful in battles fought at Kuṇṇēr, Śingalam and Viliṇam and who at Kuḍamūkkil won a deaddly battle against the combined armies of the Ganga, Pallava, Chōla, Kalinga, Magadha and other kings. Next came Varagunavarman. His younger brother was Parāntakaṇ Śaḍaiyaṇ, who fought battles at Śeṇṇilam, Kharagiri and Peṇṇāgaḍam in the Koṇgu country. To him and his queen Vāṇavaṇmahādēvi was born Rājasimiha. He later fought a battle Ulappirimaṅgalam, drove the king of Thāṇji in battle at Naippūr, won a battle at Koḍumbai, burnt the town of Vāṇji on the northern bank of the Poṇṇi (Kāvēri) river and destroyed the lord of the southern Thāṇjai at Nāval. When Rājasimiha was encamped at Chūlal to the east of Rājasimhakulam he granted to the brāhmaṇa Parāntaka, the village Naṇcheyagai-puttūr in Ala-nāḍu, renaming it Nandaraguravamaṅgalam. The viṇnappam of grant was a certain Śaḍaiya-pirāṇ-Bhattasōmayājin of Pullamaṅgalam in Chōla-nāḍu and the ājṇapti was Kūrraṅgōṇ, a native of Vembarrūr in Kaļavali-nāḍu. Nakkaṇ-kumāṇ of the village of Kūra in Kilvēmba-nāḍu was the Kuḍikāval-nāyakaṇ.
